title: "Census sections to health areas: assignment check"

    embed-resources: true
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

Covariates are built from census sections. Sections and health areas were
drawn independently and only mostly nest. Two rules move covariates across
(`helpers/census_sections.R`):

- **population** (main): a section straddling health areas is split by where its
  residents live on the GHS-POP 100 m grid (dasymetric, Pebesma & Bivand ch. 5.3);
- **point** (sensitivity): the whole section goes to the health area holding its
  point on surface (supervisor's rule).

Maps are in `figures.qmd`. Render with `quarto render reports/<file>.qmd` from the repository folder.

```{r}
#| include: false
root = normalizePath(if (dir.exists("helpers")) "." else "..")
setwd(root)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
```

```{r}
source("helpers/regions.R"); source("helpers/tables.R"); source("helpers/census_sections.R"); source("helpers/figures.R")
cat_x = section_check("catalunya")
mad_x = section_check("madrid")
```

## How well the point rule nests

Share of each section's residents living in the health area the point rule picks.

```{r}
lapply(list(catalunya = cat_x, madrid = mad_x), \(x) st_drop_geometry(x$sections) |>
	count(share_class, name = "sections")) |>
	bind_rows(.id = "region") |>
	pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = sections) |>
	knitr::kable()
```

## What the rule changes

Area covariates under both rules. Population totals are identical; points off
the 1:1 line are health areas whose covariates moved.

```{r}
cmp = list(catalunya = rule_comparison("catalunya"), madrid = rule_comparison("madrid"))
bind_rows(cmp, .id = "region") |>
	group_by(region, name) |>
	summarise(r = cor(point, population), median_abs_pct = median(abs(diff_pct)),
		areas_over_5pct = sum(abs(diff_pct) > 5), max_abs_pct = max(abs(diff_pct)), .groups = "drop") |>
	knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
plot_rule_scatter(cmp$catalunya, "Catalunya")
plot_rule_scatter(cmp$madrid, "Madrid")
```
